adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.7. A 6.2% price increase to $12.03 is a known demand-lowering driver. Past promotions at similar price points (12.03) show a median lift of x1.4 (noise-adjusted), but this week has no promotion. The recent week with the same price (2026-10-05) sold 24 units (x1.30 vs baseline), suggesting the price hike already dampened demand. The heatwave (38°C) is a plausible demand driver, but no past heatwave data exists. The classical model suggests no lift, but judgment overrides it: a heatwave in a cold/flu product category is plausible. Evidence is thin (one event, no history), so shrink toward 1.0. Price increase is confirmed, but no promotion. Combine with caution.

  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)
  planner notes: Heatwave forecast: 38°C all week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.7 | 5%-95%: 3.6 - 38.4 | 10%-90%: 7.5 - 34.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
